problem.title: Opposite the Center Face
problem.statement: A cube net has four squares A-B-C-D in a horizontal row. Square E is directly above B, and square F is directly below B. Which face is opposite B after folding?
hints: List the four faces sharing net edges with B.
A cube face has four adjacent faces and one opposite face.

solutionSteps.title: Inventory B's neighbors
solutionSteps.body: A, C, E, and F share B's four edges and fold around B.

solutionSteps.title: Use the leftover
solutionSteps.body: D is the only other face, so D is opposite B.

validationMethods: independent face-normal propagation on coordinates A(−1,0), B(0,0), C(1,0), D(2,0), E(0,1), F(0,−1) gives opposite pairs A–C, B–D, E–F; option audit

problem.title: Across the T-Net
problem.statement: A valid cube net has A-B-C in a horizontal row. D is directly above B, E is directly above D, and F is directly below B. Which face is opposite D after folding?
hints: Use B as the reference face.
D and F attach to opposite edges of B.

solutionSteps.title: Fold around B
solutionSteps.body: D folds from B's upper edge and F folds from B's lower edge, placing them on opposite faces.

validationMethods: independent normal propagation on coordinates A(0,0), B(1,0), C(2,0), D(1,1), E(1,2), F(1,−1) gives pairs A–C, B–E, D–F; option audit

problem.title: All Three Opposite Pairs
problem.statement: A valid cube net has A-B-C in a horizontal row. D is directly above B, E is directly above D, and F is directly below B. Which list gives all three pairs of opposite cube faces?
hints: Start with faces attached to opposite edges of B.
The face extended beyond D closes opposite B.

solutionSteps.title: Fold side pairs
solutionSteps.body: A and C fold to opposite sides of B, while D and F fold to another opposite pair.

solutionSteps.title: Close the cube
solutionSteps.body: E folds over the remaining side opposite B.

validationMethods: independent face-normal propagation yields exactly A–C, B–E, D–F and confirms the six faces occur once; option audit

problem.title: A New Edge After Folding
problem.statement: A cube net has A-B-C-D in a horizontal row, with E directly above B and F directly below B. Which pair does not share an edge in the flat net but does share an edge after folding?
hints: First identify the three opposite pairs.
Any two distinct cube faces that are not opposite share an edge.

solutionSteps.title: Find opposites
solutionSteps.body: The folded cube has opposite pairs A-C, B-D, and E-F.

solutionSteps.title: Test the choices
solutionSteps.body: The first three choices are opposite pairs. A and E are not opposite, so they meet along a cube edge even though their squares do not share a net edge.

validationMethods: opposite-pair elimination plus cube incidence rule
independent coordinate-normal model verifies A·C, B·D, and E·F have antiparallel normals while A and E have perpendicular normals; flat-edge audit confirms A and E are not hinged

problem.title: Fold, Then Roll Twice
problem.statement: A cube net has A-B-C-D in a horizontal row, with E directly above B and F directly below B. Fold it with B on top, A on the left, C on the right, E away from you, F toward you, and D on the bottom. Roll the cube one face to the right, then one face away from you. Which face is on top?
hints: After the right roll, the left face becomes top.
Carry every face position into the second roll.

solutionSteps.title: Roll right
solutionSteps.body: A, the left face, becomes the top; B moves right and D moves left.

solutionSteps.title: Roll away
solutionSteps.body: F, still the face toward you, rises to the top.

validationMethods: six-position orientation table updated east then north
independent inverse audit: from final top F, rolling toward then left returns top B and restores A west, C east, E north, F south, D bottom; option audit

problem.title: Staircase Net
problem.statement: Six squares form a valid staircase cube net. Starting at A, move up to B, right to C, up to D, right to E, and up to F. Which face is opposite C after folding?
hints: Track one face normal through each hinge turn.
The full opposite pairs can check your result.

solutionSteps.title: Propagate orientations
solutionSteps.body: Fold successively along the path's up, right, up, right, and up hinges.

solutionSteps.title: Pair antiparallel faces
solutionSteps.body: The resulting opposite pairs are A-D, B-E, and C-F.

validationMethods: face-normal propagation through N-E-N-E-N hinge sequence
independent cube-net embedding on coordinates A(0,0), B(0,1), C(1,1), D(1,2), E(2,2), F(2,3) yields six unique normals and opposite pairs A–D, B–E, C–F; option audit
